item.title: Noah Kahan Blown Away After Scoring First No. 1 LP on Billboard 200, (Humbly) Celebrates By Splurging on Airplane Wi-Fi: ‘Messaging Only’
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music news and trends. Today, we're celebrating a major milestone for singer-songwriter Noah Kahan. His fourth studio album, "The Great Divide", has debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 chart.
[Short music transition]
Host: Kahan, known for his contemplative pop-folk songs, took to Instagram to share the news with his fans. In a humorous post, he joked about buying the Wi-Fi package on his flight to celebrate. The Vermont native even poked fun at his own frugal ways, comparing himself to Bernie Sanders.
[Short music transition]
Host: But the numbers are no joke. "The Great Divide" earned an impressive 389,000 equivalent album units in the US, making it the largest week for a rock album since the chart began measuring by units in 2014. It's also the third-biggest week of 2026 among all albums, and Kahan's biggest week by units in his career.
[Short music transition]
Host: Kahan's team is thrilled, with his management firm's GM, Ryan Langlois, noting that he's setting records in the modern era. Kahan himself had a witty response, joking that he would have given himself more playing time in a celebrity all-star game.
[Short music transition]
Host: And if that's not enough, "The Great Divide" also debuted at number one on the Official UK albums chart, marking Kahan's second chart-topper across the pond. As he put it, "Life is crazy, and I'm grateful for it all."
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Congratulations to Noah Kahan on his well-deserved success. We'll be keeping an eye on his future projects. Thanks for listening, and we'll catch you in the next episode!
